output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a new Corvane edge rule, AUTO-LIB-17, which went live on 3 March at 10:38 UTC. It blocks password-login requests that use the app's networking library and carry no session cookie. About 41,000 installs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before, so these are real customers and not bots. The drop began within a minute of the rule going live, on every app version, every OS version and both patch states. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. Release 6.14 was only 5% of attempts and fails at the same rate as older versions. So a 6.14 rollback would not help, and neither would reverting the password screen. Raising bot sensitivity would block more real customers. Excluding blocked attempts from the KPI would hide the problem from executives. Next step: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the password-login path, keeping rate limits and lockout in place. Then confirm in telemetry that password-login success returns to about 96%. Keep the 6.14 rollout going while you track outcomes by version. Ask Corvane to route future rule updates through testing. I'm about 90% sure.
